West Pier, Brighton circa 1920. In 1916 a large concert hall was erected in the central part of the pier. After this the pier was essentially unchanged.

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition
method: Wholly original live code. First light over the pier. Pale motes leave the skeleton, settle on the swell and ride it out to sea; now and then dolphins rise among them. Nothing repeats exactly.
inspired: inspired by a memory shared on the wall by Bx
source_credit: No source image. Inspired by a memory shared on the wall by Bx, who invited it to be used.
quote: West pier has a particular significance in my life. I lived opposite in our family hotel from the age of 16. I watched the landing station fall into the sea with my brother. My mum was a save the west pier society member and campaigned for it to be saved for 40 years. They use to try and sell it to the right investor for £1 but wealthy investors were often turned down such as a Disney land. A underwater maze and recreating a Victorian feel were popular but never happened. Some argue that the purists limited the chances of its survival. We scattered my Mum and Dad’s ashes there so I like to feel they enjoyed an ashes surfer’s party with the dolphins.
